lines: An LFO with one output, sweeping continuously from sine through to narrow pulse, with modelled analog character and drift, and a clock input that locks its rate to a ratio of the tempo.
Sweeps the waveform in four equal quarters, sine to triangle to saw to square to pulse; over the last quarter the pulse narrows from 50% duty to 5%.
Crossfades each shape from clean to a modelled analog one and bleeds in the neighbouring shapes; the effect is the square of the setting, so half way gives about a quarter of it.
Scales a bundle of analog imperfections together: slow pitch wander, cycle-to-cycle timing jitter, a wandering offset on the output, and a lag on frequency changes; it is eased back while clocked.
Sets the frequency free-running, 0.01Hz to 20Hz. With a clock patched it snaps instead to one of 15 ratios of the clock, from 16 times slower to 16 times faster, with the centre at x1.
Shifts where in the cycle the output is read, 0 to 360 degrees, without moving the cycle itself.
Attenuates the MORPH input, 0 to 100%; at 100% 5V covers the whole of the MORPH knob's travel. It comes up at 0%, passing nothing.
Attenuates the CHAR input, 0 to 100%; at 100% 5V covers the whole of the CHARACTER knob's travel. It comes up at 0%, passing nothing.
Attenuates the DRIFT input, 0 to 100%; at 100% 5V covers the whole of the DRIFT knob's travel. It comes up at 0%, passing nothing.
Attenuates the FM input, 0 to 100%; at 100% a volt shifts the rate by six tenths of an octave free-running and half an octave while clocked. It comes up at 0%, passing nothing.
Attenuates the PHASE input, 0 to 100%; at 100% 5V covers the full 360 degrees. It comes up at 0%, and does nothing at all unless a cable is in the PHASE input.
Adds to the MORPH knob through the trim above it, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt at 100%, with the total held between 0 and 100%.
Adds to the CHARACTER knob through the trim above it, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt at 100%, with the total held between 0 and 100%.
Adds to the DRIFT knob through the trim above it, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt at 100%, with the total held between 0 and 100%.
Modulates the rate exponentially through the FM trim; at 100% a volt shifts it by six tenths of an octave free-running and half an octave while clocked.
Adds to the PHASE knob through the trim above it, 72 degrees per volt at 100%, with the total held between 0 and 360 degrees.
Locks the rate to the incoming tempo, registering above 1V and re-arming below 0.1V; the first pulse restarts the cycle and the lock settles after four steady pulses.
Restarts the cycle at its beginning on a rising edge above 1V, crossfading over 3ms so there is no click.
The waveform, ±5V, with the wandering offset from DRIFT added on top of it.
Note — Every CV trim comes up at 0%. A cable in MORPH, CHAR, DRIFT, FM or PHASE does nothing at all until the trim directly above that jack is raised.
Note — With CLK empty the module free-runs and RATE sets the frequency in Hz. With a clock patched RATE picks a ratio instead, and the display changes to the ratio and the tempo.
Note — A tempo that changes for several pulses in a row is followed, while a single early or late pulse is discarded, so one stray edge does not throw the lock off.
Note — The display shows the waveform, a dot at the current phase, and either the rate in Hz or the ratio, the tempo and a SYNC badge. Nothing on it can be clicked.
Menu — Swing: Straight 50%, Light 54%, Medium 58%, Triplet 66%, Heavy 71%, Max 75% — sets how far through the cycle its midpoint falls; it has no effect while free-running.

ForgeAnalogLFO.notes:
Read at commit 690ed35, 'chore: bump version to 2.0.1 for library resubmission'. The installed plugin.json is byte-identical to that commit's, and the repository has 606 commits all carrying 2.0.1 after it. Two things settled which one shipped: from 299e77c onwards plugin.json registers a second module, ForgeAnalogVCO, which the installed manifest does not list, and nm on the installed plugin.dylib returns no VCO symbols at all. Between 690ed35 and 299e77c nothing touches src/AnalogLFO.cpp, its dsp headers or res/AnalogLFO.svg, so every 2.0.1 candidate is the same LFO and 690ed35 is the earliest of them.

The DSP is written out in full in src/dsp/ (LfoCore, DriftEngine, ClockTracker, Waveshape, Swing) and nothing is vendored. Every figure above is from those files.

Index order is not panel order here. Input 1 is Drift CV and input 2 is Character CV, while the panel prints CHAR in the third column and DRIFT in the fourth, so the two are crossed relative to the enum. The tags follow the census positions: Character CV (input 2) sits at x 54.8 under CHAR, Drift CV (input 1) at x 86.9 under DRIFT.

Two places where the maker's own docs do not match the code:
- docs/engine-concept.md and docs/panel.md say the five morph shapes take 'roughly 20% each' and that 80-100% is narrow pulse. src/dsp/Waveshape.hpp:165-185 multiplies morph by 4, giving four crossfade segments of 25%: sine at 0, triangle at 25%, saw at 50%, square at 75% and pulse only at 100%, with the top quarter narrowing the duty from 50% to 5% rather than crossfading.
- docs/io-reference.md says the Phase Offset CV is 'active only when patched'. That is true, and it also means the Phase-Offset trim does nothing while that jack is empty, which nothing in the docs says.

The drift offset is added after the anti-click crossfade (src/dsp/LfoCore.hpp:236), so with DRIFT raised the output can sit a little outside ±5V. The docs describe the output as bipolar ±5V without the qualification.

Swing is gated on clocked mode in two places (src/dsp/Swing.hpp:34 and the display gate at src/AnalogLFO.cpp:344), so the menu setting is stored but inert while free-running, and the on-screen swing overlay is hidden at Straight.

The waveform display is a TransparentWidget with no ParamWidget behind it and no census position, so no click reaches it.

Each instance draws its own random spread coefficients at construction (src/AnalogLFO.cpp:226-234) and saves them in the patch, so two copies of the module are very slightly differently detuned and each one reloads with the character it had.
